solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cheating, getting twice the number going over

parts.note: twice the number is double it
going over a road or river is crossing it

explanation.surface: Someone cheats by counting twice as many while walking across something.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-crossing is betraying a partner by deceit, a form of cheating.

clue.text: Give up, trapped by unforced errors

indicators.note: the letters sit trapped inside the run of the words unforced errors

explanation.surface: A tennis player concedes the match, beaten by their own unforced errors.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or yield something, i.e. give it up.

clue.text: One to almost gamble on a bit of a looker

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to gamble is to risk

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to stake a bet on a good-looking person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a looker' is slang for an attractive person, but here it is an eye, and the iris is part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is the coloured part of the eye, and an eye is something that looks.

clue.text: First-class beer served up with all the trimmings

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI
lager is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A top-quality pint is brought out with all the extras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns AILAGER round in this down clue, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are ceremonial finery and insignia, the full trimmings of office.

clue.text: Staying away from sailor since ten got lost

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: letters that got lost are scattered, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor has been missing ever since ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is the crossword sailor; 'got lost' scrambles SINCE TEN into STINENCE, and 'Staying away' reads as the sailor's absence but defines the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinence is refraining or keeping away from something, such as drink.

clue.text: One tendering change for part of a meal

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of these letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone paying for a meal is offering money and waiting for change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like the cash handed back, but it is the anagram signal for I plus TENDERING.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingredient is one component of a dish, so a constituent part of a meal.

clue.text: Money spinner?

parts.note: read literally, a machine whose reels spin and which takes or pays out money

explanation.definitionFit: A fruit machine in a pub spins its reels and swallows coins, so it literally spins for money.

clue.text: Basic facilities that might stun RAF recruit being trained

indicators.note: being trained means being drilled into a new shape, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A new Air Force recruit in training could be stunned by the experience.
explanation.walkthrough: RAF is the Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrastructure is the underlying set of essential services such as roads and power.

clue.text: Started job working in antiques, for example

indicators.note: working means being worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has just begun a job in the antiques trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges STARTED JOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Objets d'art are decorative art objects, of which antiques are an example.

clue.text: Pitch and run after tea outside

indicators.note: after places the run letter behind the tea letters
the outside of the word tea is its first and last letters

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cricket match: the pitch, a run and then tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' takes the first and last letters of tea, TA; 'after' puts R behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch is a black sticky substance, the same thing as tar.

clue.text: Break provided in case of riot

indicators.note: in places the provided word inside the riot letters
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: provided means if, as in on condition that

explanation.surface: Something breaks if a riot happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' may look like an escape from a riot, but it is the definition; 'case of' and 'in' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A rift is a split or crack, so a break.

clue.text: Water that's got carbon in

indicators.note: in places the carbon symbol within the that's letters

parts.note: that's, meaning that is, is i.e.
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: This water has carbon in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is frozen water, so water in solid form.

clue.text: Half-decent speech award

indicators.note: half takes the first three of the six letters of decent

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A fairly decent speech wins a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoration is a medal or honour conferred, i.e. an award.

clue.text: Arranged schedule for brothers to decorate

parts.note: a religious order is a body of brothers such as monks
to paper a room is to decorate it with wallpaper

explanation.surface: A plan is drawn up for the brothers to decorate the monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: An order paper is the printed agenda of business for a day in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: An order paper sets out the arranged items of business, a schedule.

clue.text: Runs into position of advantage, being innovative

indicators.note: into places the runs letter inside the rearranged letters
the position of the letters is changed, so advantage is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A footballer runs into a good attacking position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'position of' rearranges ADVANTAGE to AVANTGADE; 'into' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant-garde means experimental and ahead of its time, so innovative.

clue.text: Stage work with not a little weight

indicators.note: not means the following letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a drama is a work for the stage

explanation.surface: A stage production carries plenty of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes A from DRAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A dram is a small unit of weight, a sixteenth of an ounce.

clue.text: Gentle girl, oddly, had a fight reported

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of girl, first and third
reported means we want a word that is said like a duel

parts.note: a duel is a fight

explanation.surface: A mild girl, strangely, was said to have got into a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes GR from girl; 'reported' gives the sound of 'a duel'. 'had' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradual slope or change is gentle, not steep or sudden.

clue.text: Understanding sailing course includes temporary accommodation

indicators.note: includes means the course letters hold the accommodation inside

parts.note: ENE, east-north-east, is a compass course a ship can sail
a tent is temporary shelter

explanation.surface: A sailing course comes with camping accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points such as ENE serve as courses in crosswords; 'includes' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations.

clue.text: Seafood concession welcoming visit

indicators.note: welcoming means the concession letters take the visit inside

parts.note: a sop is a small concession to placate someone
to call is to pay a visit

explanation.surface: A small gift is offered to welcome a visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concession' suggests a reduced-price ticket or a stall, but here it means a sop; 'welcoming' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallop is a shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Drug addict finds employment beginning to rankle

parts.note: employment of something is its use

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An addict finds that having a job begins to irritate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes R from rankle.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for someone who takes drugs habitually.

clue.text: Speculator's time away from home after parking summons

definitions.note: speculator's reads as speculator is, the 's a link

indicators.note: after places the summons word before the time and away letters

parts.note: a parking ticket is a summons for illegal parking
out means not at home

explanation.surface: A speculator is out of town when a parking fine arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: A ticket tout, in Britain, buys up event tickets and resells them at inflated prices.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket tout speculates on demand for tickets, buying cheap to sell dear.

clue.text: Link with Bangkok national, according to Listener

indicators.note: according to a listener means the word as heard, not as written

parts.note: a native of Thailand, whose capital is Bangkok, is a Thai

explanation.surface: A connection with a person from Bangkok, as a listener tells it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is also a crossword, adding a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a bond or connection, i.e. a link.

clue.text: One scoffs at one involved in film classification

indicators.note: involved in means the one letter goes inside the classification

parts.note: PG, parental guidance, is a film rating
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a person working on film ratings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffs' looks like mocking but means eats greedily; a glutton is a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig is someone who eats greedily, one who scoffs food.

clue.text: Travel document obtained by way of covering letters at last

indicators.note: covering means the via letters wrap round the other letter

parts.note: via means by way of

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of the word letters

explanation.surface: A travel permit arrives in the post, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes S from letters; 'covering' puts VIA round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an endorsement in a passport permitting entry to a country.

clue.text: Start soundly, saving some salary?

parts.note: to begin neighbouring words with the same sound, as saving, some and salary all do

explanation.definitionFit: Words that alliterate begin with the same sound, as the clue's s words show.

clue.text: Catch on a small branch

definitions.meaning: to catch on is to understand, British slang
a slender shoot of a tree

explanation.definitionFit: Twig is British slang for realise, and also a little shoot of a tree.

clue.text: A lot of pilots have time!

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is full of pilots

explanation.surface: Many pilots have plenty of free time.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft of things is a large number of them.

clue.text: Accepted discord and avarice in organising aid effort

indicators.note: in places the avarice word inside the reorganised letters
organising means putting into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
avarice is greed

explanation.surface: There was disagreement and greed in setting up the relief effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organising' rearranges AID EFFORT to ATODIFFER; 'in' puts GREED inside after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree to differ is to accept a disagreement and stop arguing.
